text:
emma_support: FYI customer PaperTrail reported sustained p99 spikes on /v1/embeddings in apac-sg3 starting ~03:40 UTC. Also seeing intermittent 401 auth errors in their logs. Opening escalated incident — tagging infra + SRE.

matt_platform: pulling dashboards now. p95 ~2x, p99 ~3.5-4x for embeddings specifically. Correlating with driver rollout window at 03:25-03:35. Traces show long wait on I/O and some requests stuck in allocate_gpu path.

anya_sre: repro steps we need? which image/kernel/driver rolled? any change to NVMe config?

diego_infra: we promoted nvidia-driver 535.86 -> 535.90 to apac pool at 03:28 UTC as part of the scheduled driver roll. Host kernel patch (6.6.3) also landed overnight on the same nodes. NVMe qdepth spikes seen on several hosts in the pool.

olivia_prod: customer logs show auth token refresh loops (401 -> retry -> 429) around same timestamps. Could be downstream effect — auth service timeouts when embed requests backpressure upstream.

matt_platform: timeline looks like: driver + kernel changes -> increased host io wait -> embed worker latency -> client retries -> auth pressure. Immediate triage suggestions: 1) isolate affected apac hosts, 2) rollback driver on a canary subset, 3) apply routing fallback to eu/na for new embed requests.

emma_support: I’ve told PaperTrail we’re routing their traffic to eu for stability and applied temporary credit. They asked for ETA on fix and RCA.

diego_infra: starting rollback on 2 canaries now (sg3-node-104, sg3-node-118). Commands:
```bash
# drain node for rollback testing
kubectl cordon sg3-node-104
kubectl drain sg3-node-104 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=30
# rollback driver via ansible playbook
ansible-playbook -i inventories/apac drivers/rollback.yml -l sg3-node-104
```

anya_sre: also toggling KV cache for canary embeddings to reduce disk hot reads: set REDWOOD_KV_CACHE=false in the canary config. This should cut some host read amplification.

matt_platform: enabling per-route traces for embeddings and collecting flamegraphs. Adding a short retention of full trace spans for 1h.

olivia_prod: auth team — can you check token service latency and 502/503 spikes between 03:30-04:00 UTC? If we see upstream timeouts, that supports retry cascade hypothesis.

deploy-bot: drivers/rollback/9965432100 initiated (canary: sg3-node-104, sg3-node-118).

diego_infra: canary rollback finished on sg3-node-104 and sg3-node-118. Observability: p95/p99 for embeddings on those nodes dropped back to baseline within 3 minutes. NVMe qdepth and iowait graphs normalized for canaries.

anya_sre: rolling out rollback to remainder of apac pool in waves of 10 nodes with 10m observation windows. Also applying a node taint to prevent scheduling until verification:
```bash
kubectl taint nodes -l region=apac latency-issue=true:NoSchedule
```

matt_platform: routing policy applied to steer 80% of new embedding traffic for PaperTrail to eu and na for 30m. Verified through rate-limiter logs.

olivia_prod: customer confirms p99 dropped on their side after reroute. They still saw intermittent auth 401s but overall request success is improved.

emma_support: noted. Customer asked for permanent mitigations and RCA.

diego_infra: immediate mitigation done (rollback + routing). Next steps: bisect driver versions across 535.x to identify the offending change; collect nvme SMART and iostat samples for affected hosts; open case with GPU vendor about driver/firmware interaction with our NVMe scheduler.

anya_sre: also scheduling kernel scheduler tuning trial (adjust mq-deadline -> bfq) and increasing NVMe queue depth caps for specific PCI lanes as a mitigatory experiment. Will run in staging first.

matt_platform: longer term: add automated host-level rollback if host p99 > SLO threshold for 3 consecutive windows; better preflight tests for driver+kernel combos that stress NVMe and KV cache patterns.

olivia_prod: auth team will send logs and correlation map to incident channel — they saw a small burst of 502s in token service coincident with the embed storm.

deploy-bot: drivers/rollback/9965432100 -> rollout to apac pool wave 1 started.

diego_infra: after 40m waves 1-3, apac pool rollback completed. Aggregate p95/p99 for embeddings in apac is now back to baseline. No further auth 401 cascades observed post-rollback and reroute.

anya_sre: mitigation checklist:
- rollback driver 535.90 -> 535.86 across apac (done)
- route policy fallback for high-latency embeds (temp)
- KV cache toggle for heavy workloads (canary verified)
- schedule kernel IO-scheduler tuning in staging
- open vendor support ticket for driver/firmware/TL; attach iostat and flamegraphs

matt_platform: I’ll own the RCA doc: include timelines, metrics, vendor ticket id, and recommended host SLO guardrails. Will propose automation for rollback on host-level SLO breaches.

emma_support: thanks. I’ll update PaperTrail with an interim RCA and ETA for full report. Closing follow-up when RCA published. :white_check_mark: cc support_lead

support_lead: great triage — please include the customer impact table and the minutes of traffic steering when you publish the RCA.

---
Note: quick repro commands used during triage (for records):
```bash
# gather top io wait hosts in apac pool\for host in $(rg "apac-sg3" hosts-list.txt -o); do ssh $host "ps -eo pid,comm,etime,%cpu --sort=-%cpu | head -n 10; iostat -x 1 3"; done
# capture nvme qdepth snapshot\ssh sg3-node-118 "cat /sys/block/nvme0n1/device/queue_depth; iostat -x 1 3" > /tmp/sg3-node-118-iostat.log
```

End of thread.
